About.title: Sentinello
About.intro: Centralized dependency-vulnerability monitoring across your portfolio — self-hosted, on your own infrastructure.
About.notDoBody: Sentinello runs entirely on your infrastructure. It never reads your application code — it discovers projects by locating the dependency manifests and lockfiles of every supported ecosystem (package.json and its lockfile for Node.js; requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, Pipfile and their lockfiles for Python; go.mod for Go; Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock for Rust; Gemfile and Gemfile.lock for Ruby) — nothing it reads leaves your machine, no telemetry is sent, there is no central account, and no LLM or AI is involved. By default it is plain npm audit for Node.js; the optional OSV and gemnasium sources (Settings → Sources, off by default) only fetch public advisory data over HTTPS.
About.whoBody: Built by <company>Walk of Code LLC</company> and Sebastian Arena (<linkedin>LinkedIn</linkedin>).
About.advisoryBody: Sentinello covers Node.js, Python, Go, Rust and Ruby. For Node.js, vulnerability data comes by default from the GitHub Advisory Database, reached through the npm registry’s advisory endpoint via npm audit. OSV and GitLab gemnasium (Settings → Sources) cover all five: for Node.js they add advisories npm audit misses and flag known-malicious packages, and for Python, Go, Rust and Ruby they are the only sources. Both are off by default, so a project in one of those four languages reads “No source enabled for …” until you turn one on. Both resolve your dependencies offline from the lockfile and match them against a locally cached copy of the advisory data, so no per-project request leaves your machine at scan time; an ambiguous manifest, or one with no lockfile, is reported as partial or unauditable rather than treated as clean. Sentinello reads only gemnasium’s own machine-readable version range — together with the fix version the record lists — to decide what an advisory affects. Each ecosystem’s versions are compared by its own rules: npm’s own semver implementation for npm, semver for crates.io, PEP 440 for Python, Go’s module versions and RubyGems’ version ordering. In OSV event ranges, an unreadable upper bound is ignored rather than allowed to silence an otherwise valid interval. A record whose range selects no version, or is written in range syntax Sentinello does not implement, is discarded rather than guessed at, and no other source is consulted to fill the gap. Fix versions are checked against each ecosystem’s own registry.

npm.purpose: Fetch advisory data via npm audit

npmRegistry.purpose: Check that a fix version was actually published, and — when none was — read the package metadata the way out is built from (releases, dependencies, deprecation notices, maintainers). Packages with findings and their dependency chains and, when no fix is released, the candidate releases and alternatives the way out weighs, with their dependency trees
npmRegistry.when: After each scan, for packages without a successful answer in the last 24 hours; a failed request is not stored, so it can be retried sooner
npmRegistry.disable: Not disableable — SENTINELLO_NPM_REGISTRY_URL points it at a mirror. When it cannot be reached, package metadata fetched earlier is reused if it is still usable, and current findings are evaluated against it, with the date it was fetched; without it, the fix shows as not checked against the registry

npmDownloads.purpose: Weekly download counts shown beside the packages and alternatives in a way out
npmDownloads.when: After a scan that finds no fixed version released, for packages not counted in the last 24 hours
npmDownloads.disable: Not disableable — SENTINELLO_NPM_DOWNLOADS_URL points it elsewhere. When it cannot be reached, the last known count is shown, or unknown when there is none

osv.purpose: Download the public OSV advisory export for each ecosystem OSV is enabled for (npm, PyPI, Go, crates.io, RubyGems)

osv.disable: Settings → Sources (off by default), or SENTINELLO_OSV_FEED_URL=off

pypi.purpose: Check that a fix version of a Python package with a finding was actually published and not yanked

About.dataLivesBody: All scan results are stored in a single local SQLite database. Under Docker it lives in the mounted volume at /app/data; running directly (for example under pm2) it defaults to data/sentinello.sqlite in the project directory. Either way you can point it elsewhere with the SENTINELLO_DB_PATH environment variable. It never leaves your machine. Scan history is pruned on the retention window set in Settings → Advanced (90 days by default); findings, mutes and notification history are kept indefinitely.
About.configBody: Sentinello is configured entirely through environment variables. Every variable and its default:

configRows.port: Port the web portal listens on inside the container.
configRows.dbPath: Location of the SQLite database; keep it on the mounted volume.
configRows.portalBaseUrl: External URL used in notification links.
configRows.meName: Display name used as the owner and mute-author label.
configRows.portalToken: When set, requires logging in at /login with this token before any route (except the health check) is reachable. Unset means no authentication.
configRows.version: Version label shown in the footer and at /api/version; baked into the image at build time.
configRows.updateFeedUrl: Feed checked for the update banner; set to off to disable update checks.
configRows.webhookStrict: When enabled, rejects webhook targets aimed at private or loopback addresses and requires https. Link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are always rejected.
configRows.osvFeedUrl: Base URL for the OSV advisory export, used only when the OSV source is enabled; set to off to disable all OSV network access.
configRows.osvDbPath: Location of the rebuildable OSV advisory cache; defaults next to the main database.
configRows.gemnasiumFeedUrl: URL for the GitLab gemnasium advisory archive, used only when the gemnasium source is enabled; set to off to disable all gemnasium network access.
configRows.gemnasiumDbPath: Location of the rebuildable gemnasium advisory cache; defaults next to the main database.
configRows.npmRegistryUrl: npm registry that fix versions are checked against after each scan, and that package metadata for the way out is read from; point it at a mirror if you use one. When it cannot be reached, package metadata fetched earlier is reused if it is still usable, and current findings are evaluated against it, with the date it was fetched; without it, the fix shows as not checked against the registry.
configRows.npmDownloadsUrl: npm download-count API, read for the weekly downloads shown in a way out. When it cannot be reached, the last known count is shown, or unknown when there is none.
configRows.pypiUrl: PyPI that fix versions of Python findings are checked against after each scan, only while a source is enabled for Python; point it at a mirror if you use one. When it cannot be reached, an earlier answer is reused with the date it was fetched; without one, the fix shows as not checked against the registry.
configRows.goproxyUrl: Go module proxy that fix versions of Go findings are checked against after each scan, only while a source is enabled for Go; point it at another proxy if you use one. When it cannot be reached, an earlier answer is reused with the date it was fetched; without one, the fix shows as not checked against the registry.
configRows.cratesIndexUrl: crates.io sparse index that fix versions of Rust findings are checked against after each scan, only while a source is enabled for Rust; point it at a mirror if you use one. When it cannot be reached, an earlier answer is reused with the date it was fetched; without one, the fix shows as not checked against the registry.
configRows.rubygemsUrl: RubyGems that fix versions of Ruby findings are checked against after each scan, only while a source is enabled for Ruby; point it at a mirror if you use one. When it cannot be reached, an earlier answer is reused with the date it was fetched; without one, the fix shows as not checked against the registry.
